Good morning! **Martin** here, delighted to bring you the news that matters
for Monday, though "delighted" might not quite be the right word, and
certainly I don't think it's quite right to give you my usual "Happy" Mondays
musical link, given the squalid scenes unfolding in Michigan.

In today's '**First Draft** ,' we'll consider how **Rep. Haley Stevens**
carried out a political betrayal for the ages, stabbing **Abdul El-Sayed** and
her own Democratic Party in the back just two days before election day, to say
she'll vote for **Mike Rogers**. Yes, that Mike Rogers: the repulsive
[Trumpist Islamophobe](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=29697730133146971)
and [shamelessly corrupt swamp creature](https://prospect.org/2026/10/29/mike-
rogerss-wife-runs-a-consultancy-that-sells-government-access/) Stevens spent
much of the year attacking. Stevens said she did it because El-Sayed told her
not to come to a unity rally. Really.

Elsewhere, there were major developments in election-related lawsuits brought
by the Trump administration as it stares defeat in the face; none of them good
for Trump, his cronies, or enablers like Rep. Stevens. Judges in **Alaska**
and **California** stood firm, for now, and that counts. There's plenty more
to take in, so let's get on to the news.

It might feel wrong to lead on Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens's gutter
treachery against her own party two days before the midterm elections, through
her surprise embrace of Trumpism and MAGA, with the verdict of a party leader
whose own support of Abdul El-Sayed in the Michigan Senate election has been
disgracefully weak.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

What the hell. _Even Chuck Schumer_ was absolutely appalled at Stevens's
actions.

**" This is a despicable betrayal from Rep. Stevens,"** the Senate Minority
Leader [said](https://x.com/chuckschumer/status/2116969707425468536).

**" Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we
know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan,
unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors."**

If for some reason you find yourself doubting Schumer's sincerity, well, he
endorsed Stevens in the primary so his own sense of betrayal, at least, is
clear. And if you don't believe Schumer about Rogers, the Republican with whom
Stevens appeared? Ask Stevens herself.
